facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin
A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin

concepts.why: The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver, epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments, and diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E are consistent with metastatic melanoma to the liver.

The presence of epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments, and diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E are consistent with primary hepatic melanoma, although this is a rare entity.

The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver and elevated liver enzymes are consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma, although the immunohistochemical staining pattern is not typical for this diagnosis.

rationales.F09: Multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver suggest metastasis or primary liver cancer.
rationales.F10: Epithelioid tumor cells with melanin pigments are characteristic of melanoma.
rationales.F11: Positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E is diagnostic of melanoma.
rationales.F12: Negativity for cytokeratin rules out carcinomas, including hepatocellular carcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E, along with negativity for cytokeratin and the presence of intracytoplasmic melanin pigments, strongly supports metastatic melanoma to the liver.
